Priya K (ML Eng): Quick report — onboarding magnet-32k-int4: reproducible off-by-nibble alignment causing token slips after long prefills. Minimal repro below.
Omar B: Slip meaning token IDs shifted vs fp16?
Priya K (ML Eng): Exactly. fp16: "... 7201,7202,7203,7204" int4-packed: "... 7201,7203,7204,7205" — single-token downstream slip.
Theo M: Please paste the run command and any kv flags.
Priya K (ML Eng): Run: ```bash
python -m bench.run --model magnet-32k-int4 --prefill tests/long/30k_doc.txt \ --context-window 65536 --kv-prefill-stride 256 --kv-slot-pad 32 --quant int4-packed --seed 11
```
Priya K (ML Eng): Happened on dev-gpu1 and dev-gpu3, single and multi-shard. Repro ~10/80.
Omar B: Can you dump the raw packed bytes and unpacked nibble sequence near offending slot?
Priya K (ML Eng): Hex snippet: `ab 4f 00 1e ff 10 77 ...` Unpacked nibbles (expected): `5,2,8,0,7` failing runs show a one-nibble left shift starting at slot offset 4095.
Theo M: Sounds like signed vs unsigned arithmetic when computing nibble index. We had a long tail of signed-index hacks in the legacy unpackor. Try casting index to uint32 before >> 1.
Priya K (ML Eng): Did that locally — ran 50 repeats, 0/50 repro. With kv-slot-pad 64 the repro rate drops but not zero. Will open RDW-8312 with patch and fuzz harness.
Build Bot: bench/fuzz-int4 #462 queued.
Theo M: Good. Also add an assert in debug builds for slot_offset % 2 == expected and a metric `kv_nibble_misalignment` when we detect a mismatch.
Priya K (ML Eng): Will do, filing RDW-8312 and attaching failing logs. Thanks.
